note: Curated, general-purpose libraries per capability tag. `rank` is OUR priority when several serve the same capability (higher first): a focused, exact library before a large toolkit. DATA, not code: a new game needs a new row here at most, never a branch in the harness (rulebook 3.7). 'baked' entries are installed into the image, so they also work with no network. 'why' is printed in report.json for the live demo. Nothing here is specific to one game.

entries.name: numpy
entries.why: arrays and vectorised dynamic programming: value iteration, pattern matrices, payoff matrices

entries.name: scipy
entries.why: scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS) solves a zero-sum matrix game exactly; minimize for best responses

entries.name: nashpy
entries.why: equilibria of a bimatrix game (support enumeration, Lemke-Howson, fictitious play)

entries.name: python-sat
entries.why: SAT solvers (minisat/glucose) to keep only the hidden states consistent with all feedback so far

entries.name: rank-bm25
entries.why: BM25 retrieval over the passages of a document, for answer-from-the-document games

entries.name: rapidfuzz
entries.why: fast fuzzy matching: catches a forbidden subject written with typos or spacing tricks

entries.name: Unidecode
entries.why: transliterates unicode to ASCII, so a forbidden word cannot hide behind lookalike characters

entries.name: regex
entries.why: unicode-aware regular expressions with fuzzy matching, stronger than re for outgoing-text filters

entries.name: chess
entries.why: legal move generation, FEN/SAN parsing and a UCI driver for chess-like variants (python-chess)

entries.name: treys
entries.why: fast 5-7 card poker hand evaluation for equity by Monte Carlo

entries.name: pokerkit
entries.why: poker state machine and hand evaluation for many betting variants

entries.name: z3-solver
entries.why: SMT solver: arithmetic constraints over hidden numbers, not just boolean ones

entries.name: ortools
entries.why: CP-SAT and linear solvers for assignment, allocation and consistency problems

entries.name: open-spiel
entries.why: reference implementations of CFR, MCTS and exact solvers for many abstract games

entries.name: axelrod
entries.why: a library of repeated-game strategies and tournaments, for classifying a repeated opponent

entries.name: wordfreq
entries.why: word frequency priors, so a word-guessing game starts from likely words

entries.name: networkx
entries.why: graph algorithms (matching, flows, shortest paths) for board and allocation structures
